rules.sentence: In the US, CTEPH's incidence after the initial pulmonary embolism event ranges from 0.1% to 9.1%.[17]
A meta-analysis showed that <1% of all patients with a prior diagnosis of pulmonary embolism have CTEPH at the population level.

CTEPH is frequently misdiagnosed, and its prevalence is underestimated due to limited clinician awareness and the so-called "honeymoon period"—the time interval between pulmonary embolism episodes and the onset of CTEPH symptoms.[18]
Patients with CTEPD have similar symptoms, perfusion defects, and pulmonary vessel obstructions with or without pulmonary hypertension at rest.
CTEPD is estimated to be present in 20% of individuals suspected of CTEPH.[19]
According to the generally accepted theory, CTEPH emerges following one or multiple pulmonary embolism episodes, predominantly from venous thrombosis.[20]

This hypothesis may explain why up to 63% of patients with CTEPH do not have a history of acute pulmonary embolism (see Image. Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension Proposed Pathophysiology).[21]
